transcript.text: Beko vented dryer, drum goes round fine but it's just blowing cold air. Had it about 6 years. What part do I need?

The most likely failed part is the heater element, or the thermal cut-out/thermostat fitted with it. However, don’t buy one yet: restricted airflow is a common reason a vented dryer cuts the heat, and it can damage the replacement as well. 1. With the dryer switched off and unplugged, clean the fluff filter thoroughly. Remove lint from the filter housing too.
2. Check the vent hose from the rear to outside: it should not be crushed, sharply kinked or packed with fluff. Clear it if needed. Poor airflow can operate the thermal cut-out.
3. Check that a normal heated programme is selected — not Air/Refresh/Cool or a low-heat setting.
4. Run a normal cotton/high-heat programme for 10–15 minutes. If there is still airflow but it remains completely cold, the heater circuit is the leading suspect: usually the heater element, thermal cut-out or cycling thermostat rather than the drum motor. If the filter and hose are clear and it is still cold, an engineer can test the heater circuit safely with the machine isolated and identify which component has gone open-circuit. The exact part depends on the full model number from the rating label, so it is not safe to choose a heater from the brand and age alone.

Did all that. Filter was fairly full and the hose had a sag full of fluff, cleaned both out. Airflow is decent now but still cold after 20 min. Model says DV7110 on the front, can't get at the rear label as it's wedged in an alcove. Which part is it?

The most likely fault is now in the heater circuit. Given the previously restricted filter and hose, the thermal cut-out/thermostat is slightly more suspicious; it may have opened when the dryer overheated. The heater element itself is also a very common cause of a vented dryer tumbling normally but staying completely cold. So the honest answer is: it is most likely the heater assembly circuit — either the thermal cut-out or the element — but those two faults feel identical in use. DV7110 is a series reference, not enough to safely select an exact replacement part. The confirming check is with the dryer unplugged and pulled out: a competent person can remove the appropriate rear panel and test the isolated heater element and thermal cut-out for continuity. An open-circuit cut-out points to the cut-out/thermostat; an open-circuit element points to the heater element. Because the vent was blocked, the airflow route should remain clear before any repair, otherwise a replacement cut-out can fail again. If you cannot get it out of the alcove or do not have a meter, this is a sensible engineer job: ask them to test the heater element and thermal cut-outs, rather than replacing parts on guesswork.

candidates: Heater element or its thermal cut-out/thermostat (high)
Restricted airflow causing an overheat cut-out (medium)
